title: Chicago Sky calls Enes Kanter Freedom’s lawsuit ‘meritless and frivolous’
content:
Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter responded Friday to a lawsuit filed a day earlier by former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom, a vocal opponent of transgender athletes’ participation in women’s sports.

“We received word that the entity owning the Chicago Sky is being sued by Mr. Enes Kanter Freedom for allegedly violating his First Amendment rights. This lawsuit is meritless and frivolous,” Alter said in a statement.

Freedom’s lawsuit, which was filed in the U.S District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, alleges the Sky ejected him while he was “peacefully exercising” his right to free speech as he sat courtside at an Aug. 23 game between the Sky and Indiana Fever, wearing a T-shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” Sky guard Natasha Cloud shouted at him mid-game, and Freedom stood and argued, taking a step toward the court before security escorted him out of the building.

The Sky banned him indefinitely shortly after, though Alter later said the franchise might reconsider Freedom’s ban “if someday he’s able to demonstrate he’s capable of being at a game and conducting himself in compliance with our rules and not be a threat to people.”

In Friday’s statement, Alter said, “Freedom’s claim that he was removed from Wintrust Arena due to his speech is false. As his own complaint acknowledges, he wore the shirt in question for multiple hours without any contact with security. Security removed Freedom only after he violated fan code of conduct by rising from his seat, gesturing at a player, and stepping toward the court.

“Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech. We look forward to the truth prevailing in court.”

Freedom recently attempted to declare for the 2027 WNBA draft in a protest against trans women competing in the league, claiming in an X post that his actions “stand for women and defend free speech.” The league confirmed he is not eligible to play in the league, stating, “There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others.”

In his lawsuit, Freedom is seeking a declaration that his First Amendment rights were violated, that his indefinite ban from Wintrust Arena be lifted and that his legal fees are covered, as well as “an award of nominal and compensatory damages.”

The Sky’s statement Thursday said the franchise will have “no further public comments on the matter outside of the courtroom.”

Cloud, who called Freedom “irrelevant” in her first media availability after the altercation, said there are bigger problems facing the WNBA and women’s sports than trans athletes.

“The men now that are like ‘Oh, we need to protect the WNBA,’ y’all were the same ones saying we shouldn’t be paid,” Cloud said at the time. “Y’all were the same ones saying we shouldn’t have been invested in, saying we’re a joke, the same ones that don’t respect Black women.

“So, if you’re going to protect women, that means all women. That includes Black women, trans women, and the list goes on.”
